manualProxySub: Configure your applications to use the proxy at {address}.
heroOnTransparent: Combining {n} links for the whole PC (transparent mode)
heroOnProxy: Combining {n} links for apps using the Windows proxy
heroOffSub: Windows uses its normal connection. Press the button to combine your links.
oneLinkWarn: Only one link is connected, so there is nothing to combine. If Wi‑Fi drops when the phone is plugged in over USB, turn on “Keep Wi‑Fi with USB tethering” in Settings.
dlLead: Downloads one file over all links at once: their speeds add up.
historyLead: Data received through each link, per day.
settingsLead: How dualnet captures traffic, and the Windows settings that help it.
tunOn: Captures all the PC’s IPv4 traffic (games, downloads, browser…) with a virtual network adapter.
tunOff: Off. Captures all the PC’s traffic with a virtual network adapter, no app settings needed.
tunNeedAdmin: Needs dualnet to run as administrator.
sysOurs: On: apps that follow the Windows proxy (Edge, Chrome…) go through dualnet.
sysOther: Another proxy is set ({s}); turning this on replaces it until dualnet closes.
sysOff: Off. Points the Windows proxy to dualnet; restored when dualnet closes.
howBrowser: Firefox: Settings → Network → Manual proxy → SOCKS v5, tick “Proxy DNS when using SOCKS”.
simOn: Windows keeps Wi‑Fi connected when the phone is plugged in.
simOff: By default Windows drops Wi‑Fi as soon as a wired connection (USB tethering) appears.
needAdmin: Needs dualnet to run as administrator.
preferSub: For traffic that does not go through dualnet.
autoSub: Opens dualnet in the notification area when you sign in, without a UAC prompt.
appsNeedTun: Per-application statistics and rules need transparent mode (run dualnet as administrator and turn it on).
rulesHead: Restrict an application to one link
rulesSub: Example: keep an online game on Wi‑Fi for a steady ping while your downloads use every link. If the chosen link is down, the application uses the others. Transparent mode only.
budgetPrompt: Monthly data budget for {n} in GB (0 = none). Counts the data that goes through dualnet on this link; when it is used up, dualnet stops sending it new connections until next month.
notifSub: A Windows notification when a link drops, comes back or appears, even if this window is closed.
diagSub: Version, links and the latest log lines. Check it before sharing publicly: it lists your network interface names and addresses.
updSub: Asks GitHub for the latest release once a day. Nothing is downloaded or installed automatically.
chkSub: Checks administrator rights, links, Windows settings, the virtual adapter and the internet. Nothing is changed unless you press a Fix button.
onbSub: A few things to set up so dualnet works at its best.
chk.admin.no: Not running as administrator: transparent mode is unavailable (proxy mode still works).
chk.links.ok: {n} links are usable: they can be combined.
chk.links.one: Only one usable link: there is nothing to combine.
chk.links.none: No usable link: dualnet cannot reach the internet.
chk.link.noanswer: {name}: connected but not reaching the internet.
chk.link.budget: {name}: monthly budget used, no new connections are sent to it.
chk.wifi.ok: Windows keeps Wi‑Fi connected next to a wired link.
chk.wifi.warn: By default Windows drops Wi‑Fi when the phone is plugged in over USB.
chk.wifi.info: Windows may drop Wi‑Fi when a wired link appears; both links work for now.
chk.tun.missing: Transparent mode should be active but the virtual adapter is missing.
chk.proxy.stale: The Windows proxy points to dualnet although dualnet is not using it.
chk.proxy.ok: The Windows proxy does not point to a stopped dualnet.
chk.net.ok: DNS and internet work through the system route.
chk.net.fail: Internet check through the system route failed: {err}.
chk.exe.info: dualnet runs as administrator from {dir}: keep it in a folder only administrators can modify (for example C:\Program Files\dualnet).
chk.data.fail: Cannot write to the data folder {dir}: {err}.
chk.webview.no: WebView2 is not installed: the interface opens in your browser.
chk.autostart.off: dualnet does not start with Windows.
linksSub: Measure the real speed of each link. dualnet uses the result at once to decide how many connections each link gets.
speedNote: A test downloads for about 7 seconds from Cloudflare (up to a few hundred MB on a fast link). It goes through the link, so it counts toward the monthly budget and respects the speed cap.
roleOverflow: Only when the others are busy
roleHelp: “Only when the others are busy” keeps a link idle, for example your phone’s mobile data, until the other links are nearly full. Then dualnet adds it, and lets it go again when the load falls. A program restricted to it by a rule still uses it.
